correctness.rationale: The determinant formula for the bracket gives the automorphism condition P e1=det(P)e1 and hence the stated block group. A symbolic substitution verifies that every endomorphism is Nijenhuis. In characteristic not 2, every nonscalar involution has a 1+2 eigenspace decomposition, and both eigenspaces are automatically abelian 3-Lie subalgebras. The characteristic line Ke1 is preserved by every automorphism, and the induced SL2 action plus top-row shears is transitive on each of the three incidence types for each eigenspace dimension. Explicit normal forms, mixed-bracket tests, and finite-field replays over F3 and F5 verify the classification and counts.

originality.rationale: The 2017 exact-object source defines product structures, proves the eigenspace criterion, and gives only three illustrative matrices in Example 5.22. Two of those matrices are in the same automorphism orbit, and the generic incidence orbit is not represented. The 2021 exact-object source states that all linear maps are Nijenhuis but gives no involution quotient. Focused semantic index and literature searches located no complete product-structure orbit classification or finite-field census for this algebra.
residual_risks: A later or unindexed paper may classify product structures on the same algebra under different terminology.
The characteristic-two case is deliberately excluded and could have a different orbit geometry.
Failed searches do not prove novelty.

value.rationale: The algebra is the unique nontrivial three-dimensional 3-Lie algebra and is the canonical low-dimensional example in the product-structure literature. A complete automorphism quotient is a natural moduli refinement of the published example list, and it reveals that two published examples are the same orbit while a third geometric orbit type is absent. The strong/perfect/generic trichotomy and the exact finite-field census make the classification structurally reusable rather than an arbitrary matrix exercise.
